title: Anthropic Delivers Massive News to Stock Market Investors
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc works through Anthropic's S-1 prospectus, filed ahead of a mid-November IPO, through the lens of an investor in the companies serving Anthropic — Alphabet, Amazon, Nvidia, AMD and others — not as a would-be Anthropic buyer. The figures are stark: revenue rose from $41 million in 2023 to $4.6 billion in 2025, and in the six months to 30 June it reached $16.3 billion, up from $1.16 billion a year earlier — growth of more than ten times, closer to fifteen. Costs are rising much more slowly than revenue: compute and infrastructure costs rose roughly four to four-and-a-half times, from $2.3 billion to $8.9 billion, and total operating expenses about six times, $3.3 billion to $17 billion, so the operating loss narrowed from $2.1 billion to $693 million. He also likes the breadth behind the growth: more than 10,000 customers now spend over $100,000 a year, against earlier reports of heavy customer concentration, which he argues makes the model more sustainable and feeds a virtuous cycle for the suppliers renting Anthropic compute under its asset-light model. On the IPO itself, rumoured at a $1.5–2 trillion market value against perhaps $40–50 billion of 2026 revenue — roughly 30 times sales, cheap next to SpaceX's ~90 times at its IPO — he is clear that he will not buy at the IPO, preferring to let the market digest the figures. No explicit call is made on any ticker; Amazon and Alphabet earnings on 28–29 October are his next checkpoint.
